text:
anya: heads-up — seeing a regression in function-call JSON validity when running AWQ-8 on gpt-neox-20b replica under the toolcall-suite-v2 eval. pass rate dropped 98% -> 86%

samira: ouch. is this only AWQ or also other quant methods?

anya: quick summary: FP16 baseline 98.4% valid JSON for tool args. AWQ (group=64, bits=8) shows 86.1%. GPTQ/INT8 experiments are between 92-95%. FP8 (experimental lib) is closer to FP16 but flaky on long sequences.

devon: can you paste one small failure sample?

anya: sure — model should return a single JSON object in tools call but we get missing-quote / trailing-comma in some runs. small example:

```
Assistant: {
  "tool": "search",
  "args": {
    "query": "price of GPU",
    "filters": {
      "region": "us-west",
    }
  }
}
```

anya: note the trailing comma after "us-west" — absent in FP16 runs.

cheng: interesting. do we have tokenization differences or extra whitespace? could be rounding producing different generation boundary.

samira: i wonder if beam/temperature or sampling randomness is exposing edge tokens around the closing brace. what decode params used?

anya: eval harness used greedy, max_new_tokens=128, temperature=0.0, stop tokens set to ["\n\n"]. same config across runs.

devon: where does AWQ apply per-channel vs per-tensor? group size 64 might cause different logits distribution at end-of-sequence. try group=128 and group=32 to see trend.

anya: running +/- group sizes now. also toggling clamp and outlier clipping (awq options).

infra-bot: scheduled job: awq-group-variations-1778901234 started on runner-5 (cmd: ./eval_toolcalls --model gpt-neox-20b --quant awq --group 128)

samira: also try disable prefix caching, maybe KV cache numeric drift interacts with quantization rounding. remove cache with --no-kv-cache flag for one run.

anya: good call. i'll run a quick controlled set: FP16 baseline, AWQ g=64, AWQ g=128, AWQ g=32, AWQ g=64 + no-kv-cache, GPTQ baseline.

devon: are we logging logits sequence around the JSON close? that might show a softmax spike misaligned. put token ids and probs for the last 12 tokens.

anya: added that to the harness. sample output (AWQ g=64):

```
... token_ids: [210, 498, 7, 301, 13]
probs: [0.42, 0.17, 0.12, 0.10, 0.03]
next_tokens: [125, 34]
generated: '"us-west",\n'  <-- extra comma token present
```

cheng: looks like the model predicts a comma token where FP16 predicts closing brace. small shifts in top-k lead to syntactic break. could be quantization shifting logit ordering.

samira: mitigation ideas: 1) post-process model output with strict JSON repair (cheap but hides regression) 2) tune AWQ group/clip to recover syntactic fidelity 3) fallback to FP16 model for function-call endpoints 4) add termination discriminator that forces close-brace token if pattern matches.

anya: i prefer option 2 for production (reduce regression at source) + option 4 as temporary safety.

devon: also try bias-correction during quantization (per-channel zero-point adjust). AWQ has an experimental bias-fix flag. worth testing.

anya: running bias-fix + group=128 now. will report.

infra-bot: job awq-group-128-biasfix-1778901234 completed: 1700 samples, json-valid=95.8% (was 86.1%)

anya: promising — bias-fix recovers most errors. need to run full sweep across different prompt lengths and tool arg shapes.

samira: ok good. for rollout plan — do not promote AWQ-8 to dedicated serving for toolcall-heavy routes until we finalize config. add canary that routes toolcall endpoints to FP16 variant by default.

devon: we should also add a small unit in the eval suite that checks for exact brace-closure token sequence for function calls. add it to toolcall-suite-v2 so future quant changes catch this early.

anya: created quick PR to harness: https://git.redwood/eng-ml/toolcall-suite/pull/42 — adds token-level syntactic check and logs top-5 tokens on failure.

samira: thanks. i'll open an infra ticket to add a canary route and add config to dedicated autoscaling to pin FP16 on toolcall routes.

anya: filing ticket now. assigning to devon and cheng to follow up on quantization patches.

devon: i'll consolidate experiment results and write a short bakeoff doc with recommended AWQ flags (group=128, bias-fix=true, clip=1e-2) vs GPTQ defaults.

cheng: can we also test sequence-len=1024 vs 2048? kv-cache drift might amplify.

anya: noted. adding that to sweep.

deploy-bot: incident-preventative: Added route-rule: /v1/tools -> prefer fp16-fallback for 48h (reason: quant-json-regression)

samira: nice. keep me posted on final numbers, but bias-fix + group tuning looks like a practical fix.

anya: will close with final numbers tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:
